summary: AI observability matters because LLM applications are non-deterministic, costly, and prone to issues like hallucinations, latency spikes, and runaway token spend that are invisible without proper tracing and monitoring. As adoption accelerates in 2026 (New Relic alone reports 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring), teams rely on observability tools to trace workflows, evaluate output quality, control costs, and debug production failures. The right tool turns opaque model behavior into actionable insight, protecting both reliability and budget.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM application traces, prompt/response pairs, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics—especially tightly integrated with the LangChain framework.
features: Deep tracing of chains, agents, and tool calls
tools.pricing: Free tier available; paid plans around £80/month (~$99) for production usage—roughly 4x more expensive than Helicone for comparable request volumes.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph that want rich, framework-native tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token usage, per-user and per-department cost, latency, and caching—acting as a lightweight proxy in front of your LLM provider.
features: Best-in-class cost tracking and spend governance
Request caching to reduce API calls
tools.pricing: Free: 10K requests/month. Growth: ~£20/$20 per month for 100K requests (Pro ~$79 at 100K traces per some reports). Cheapest option—about 4x cheaper than LangSmith.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the simplest setup and the best, cheapest cost tracking regardless of framework.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment tracking, model evaluations, prompt iterations, and production application performance via the Weave product.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation with W&B Weave
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are consumption/seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML teams that want to unify traditional experiment tracking with LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production and offline LLM/ML performance, drift, data quality, embeddings, RAG quality, and evaluation—built on OpenTelemetry standards.
features: Open-source Phoenix tracing with OpenTelemetry integration
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free and open-source; Arize AX enterprise platform uses custom/consumption-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) observability with strong RAG and drift evaluation.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, evaluations, and user feedback—available as open-source self-hosted or managed cloud.
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for <50K events, then ~£20/$20 for 500K; self-hosted is free software (~£30 infra + ~2 hrs/month maintenance).
tools.best_for: Self-hosted or cost-conscious teams wanting open-source control over their observability data.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and costs using open standards (OpenTelemetry), exportable to any compatible observability backend.
features: Exports to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source (SDK by Traceloop); costs come only from your chosen backend/observability destination.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., via Helicone or a semantic cache) so identical prompts don't incur repeated API charges.
Right-size your model: route simple tasks to smaller/cheaper models and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, using a gateway like Portkey or Helicone.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, limiting context/history, and setting sensible max_output_token limits—tokens are billed both in and out.
Set per-user, per-feature, and per-department spend tracking with alerts and rate limits to catch runaway costs before they compound.
